children.translated_text: Perpetual salutation to <s>Śiva</s>, the performer of the <s>pañcakṛtya</s> (five acts),
who manifests the supreme reality that is His own Self, a dense mass of consciousness and bliss. // 1 //

children.text: citiḥ svatantrā viśvasya hetur ity abhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Citi</s> (absolute consciousness), being autonomous, is declared to be the cause of the universe;

children.text: svātantryarūpā jñātā ca siddhīr vā saṃprayacchate // 2 //
children.translated_text: having the nature of freedom, She, being the knower, bestows <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural attainments) as well. // 2 //
She, upon Her own canvas, by Her own will alone, for the unfolding of the universe,
[manifests] in the diversity of manifold forms, through the differentiation of <s>grāhya</s> (object) and <s>grāhaka</s> (subject). // 3 //
The diversity of that universe is established through the differentiation of <s>grāhya</s> (objects),
and through the variety of manifold forms, in the enumeration of higher and lower [categories]. // 4 //
From the contraction of <s>citi</s> (universal consciousness), <s>citta</s> (individual mind) arises; yet the conscious being is [in truth] <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord);

children.text: vaṭadhanikāvat tatra viśvarūpaṃ ca tad viduḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: like a banyan seed, therein the form of the entire universe — thus the wise know. // 5 //
<s>Caitanya</s> (pure consciousness) is the nature of the Self, pure and utterly immaculate;

children.text: tad eva niyamāsaktaṃ cittaṃ cid abhidhīyate // 6 //
children.translated_text: that very [consciousness], when attached to limitation, is called <s>citta</s> (mind) or <s>cit</s> (cognition). // 6 //
When <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness), turned toward objects, comes to rest in the <s>citta</s> (mind),
due to the predominance of its contracted nature, the wise know <s>citi</s> (consciousness) as <s>citta</s> (mind). // 7 //
The <s>māyā-pramātṛ</s> (knower under <s>Māyā</s>), though of the nature of consciousness, because of being identified with that [<s>Māyā</s>], in embodied beings
exists attached to sense-objects, devoid of true discrimination. // 8 //
The eternally one, established [Self], [appears as] <s>citta</s> (mind) through <s>kalā</s>, <s>sattva-guṇa</s>, and the rest,
in the form of the <s>pramātṛsaptaka</s> (seven knowers), within the enumeration of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles). // 9 //
The one, all-pervading, pure <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord), whose nature is perfect awakening —
from the recognition of that very I-consciousness, liberation stands in the palm of one's hand. // 10 //
Through the <s>pramātṛsaptaka</s> (sevenfold knower), within the enumeration of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>,
that <s>Maheśāna</s> (Great Lord) is contemplated; [thereby] the splendor of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) comes forth. // 11 //

children.text: tadbhūmikā darśanādyās sarvā eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The stages such as perception and the rest are all His stages — there is no doubt;

children.text: bhūmikāḥ kṛtrimā yadvan naṭo gṛhṇāti svecchayā // 12 //
children.translated_text: just as an actor assumes artificial roles by his own will, // 12 //
even so, expanded by the spontaneous surge of <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss),
the Self assumes the vast powers such as perception and the rest. // 12 //
The Self, radiant with the exuberant delight of <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss), shines forth;
[yet] like consciousness [itself], through the contraction of its own power, it becomes impure in <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). // 13 //
'I am incomplete' — by various <s>malas</s> (impurities) it is rendered impure,
by those called <s>māyīya</s>, <s>āṇava</s>, and <s>kārma</s> — even though it is all-pervading, the Lord of the universe. // 15 //
Just as the all-pervading <s>Mahādeva</s> (Great God) performs the <s>pañcakṛtya</s> (five acts),
even so this very Self performs [them], though deluded by <s>Śakti</s> (power). // 16 //
Through the expansion of <s>Śakti</s> (power), He is celebrated as the Lord of <s>Śakti</s> by the knowers of truth;
through contraction, He becomes contracted and is called a <s>saṃsārī</s> (transmigrating being). // 17 //

children.text: māyā rūpaṃ hi yat kiṃcid ālokayitum udyatā /
children.translated_text: Whatever form of <s>Māyā</s> [<s>citi</s>] is intent upon beholding,

children.text: sādhyasṛṣṭiṃ vijānīyād anyā śaktiḥ sthitir matā // 18 //
children.translated_text: one should know that as the creation to be accomplished; the other power is considered to be maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>). // 18 //
Through dissolution, the <s>Devī</s> (Goddess) is dissolved; in unity with consciousness, [that is] considered grace (<s>anugraha</s>);
from the non-manifestation of that unitary essence, [the fifth act] is called concealment (<s>tirodhāna</s>). // 19 //
Thus, always present is this sequence of the five activities in order;
when known, it is a wish-fulfilling gem; through ignorance, [it appears] like wood or a clod of earth. // 20 //
One who, by the strength of true <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective self-awareness), constantly cultivates [this knowledge] thus,
is liberated from all bondage and becomes full of eternal bliss. // 21 //

children.text: cidvahnir grasate so 'yaṃ suprabuddho 'sty asau yadā /
children.translated_text: The <s>cidvahni</s> (fire of consciousness) — it devours [all]; when one is fully awakened,
then one should know that pure [fire] as the <s>cidvahni</s> (fire of consciousness), the all-consuming. // 22 //
Endowed with the strength of this [fire], the <s>yogī</s> attains the characteristic of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (final liberation),

children.text: padaṃ prāpnoti vimalaṃ so 'cirān nātra saṃśayaḥ // 23 //
children.translated_text: reaching the stainless state without delay — there is no doubt in this. // 23 //
When the <s>cidvahni</s> (fire of consciousness) gains strength, the universe shines forth as pervaded by consciousness,
surging outward as waves of the nectar of one's own bliss. // 24 //

children.text: tad eva śyānatāṃ yātaṃ bhāvarūpair vibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: That very [bliss], having become dense, is experienced through the forms of [all] entities;
one's own Self, the divine <s>Maheśvara</s>, the supreme Lord, plays [as the universe]. // 25 //

children.text: iti yaḥ satataṃ vetti sa mukto mocayaty api /
children.translated_text: One who knows this constantly is liberated and liberates also
the multitude of beings in an instant from the terrible bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration). // 26 //
Whoever is empowered by [this] bliss is established in the state of one's own true nature;
thus, for one who shines with the arising of exuberant delight, // 27 //
for that one established in one's own true nature, even in the state of worldly activity (<s>vyutthāna</s>), that [realization] is attained;
this is achieved by people through the power of [their own] effort. // 28 //
Through the expansion of the <s>madhyadhāma</s> (central channel), [the light] of <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss) shines forth;
from that illumination, a divine vision, whose nature is knowledge, is experienced. // 29 //
Stainless, supremely radiant, pure, filled with eternal bliss, supreme —
even beyond the network of bodily limitations, the vision of knowledge expands forth. // 30 //
For the expansion of the <s>madhyadhāman</s> (middle channel), the means is forceful abiding;
cessation of <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs), contraction, expansion, and so on—these are manifold. // 31 //
By thinking of nothing at all, the cessation of <s>vikalpas</s> (mental constructs) comes about;
from the awakening of <s>cit</s> (consciousness), the radiant <s>Śakti</s>, impassioned, [shines forth] in the sphere of existence. // 32 //
Absorbed therein, one beholds the <s>divyaugha</s> (divine current), pure in essence;
this is indeed called <s>śaktisaṅkoca</s> (contraction of Śakti) by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. // 33 //
Resting at the extremities of beginning and end, <s>bindu</s> (point), <s>nāda</s> (resonance), and <s>laya</s> (dissolution)—likewise,
adopting [the dispositions of] fearlessness, fear, anger, disgust, and so forth— // 34 //
Thus has been described, O <s>Devī</s>, the expansion of the <s>madhyadhāman</s> (middle channel);

children.text: tatra śakto dinair evaṃ prapnoti parasampadam // 35 //
children.translated_text: one who is capable therein attains the supreme state within [a few] days. // 35 //
One who, bearing the inner impression of <s>samādhi</s>, moves among those of pure radiance—

children.text: sa visargabalād eva vimṛśya ca punaḥ punaḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: he, by the force of <s>visarga</s> (emanation) alone, reflecting again and again, // 36 //
even in <s>vyutthāna</s> (the state of emergence from meditation), his own essential nature shines forth—
of the <s>yogin</s> established in awakening, who is of the essence of eternal bliss. // 37 //
That [state], consisting of light and bliss, nourished by the power of <s>mantra</s>,
is full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhantā</s>) and pure awareness (<s>cit</s>)—for one devoted to the inner effulgence. // 38 //
There, that radiant <s>yogin</s>, established in the state of <s>Mantreśvara</s> (Lord of Mantras),

children.text: tatra śakto vibhur yadvat krīḍate śaktibṛṃhitaḥ // 39 //
children.translated_text: being capable there, the all-pervading one, nourished by <s>Śakti</s>, plays [freely] as he wills. // 39 //
Thus the sovereignty of that all-pervading Lord of the universe,
who assumes manifold distinctions and abides in wondrous states, remains unbroken. // 40 //

children.text: etad advayam ity uktaṃ jñānāmṛtam anuttamam /
children.translated_text: This has been declared the unsurpassed nectar of knowledge (<s>jñānāmṛta</s>), which is non-dual;
whoever drinks it, for him the delirium [caused by] the poison of <s>saṃsāra</s> is pacified. // 41 //
This teaching for the effulgence of awakening, for the attainment of <s>Śiva</s> by great souls—
is the perfectly pure treatise of the king named <s>Kṣema</s> [i.e., <s>Kṣemarāja</s>]. // 42 //

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the yoga treatise called <s>Bodhavilāsa</s> (The Play of Awakening), composed by the illustrious <s>Kṣemarāja</s>.
